audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for ancestral-god traditions, Abraham migration, Exodus memory, Balaam blessing, land-gift theology, choose-this-day confession, Joshua's warning against easy commitment, covenant stone witness, Joshua's death, Joseph's bones, and Eleazar's death.

verses.restored: Joshua gathered all tribes of Israel to Shechem and called elders of Israel, its heads, judges, and officers, and they stationed themselves before Divine.

modern.text: Then Joshua assembled all the tribes of Israel at Shechem. He summoned the elders, leaders, judges, and officers of Israel, and they presented themselves before God.

verses.restored: Joshua said to all people, Thus says YHWH Divine of Israel: Across the River your fathers dwelt from old, Terah father of Abraham and father of Nahor, and they served other gods.

modern.text: And Joshua said to all the people, “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Long ago your fathers, including Terah the father of Abraham and Nahor, lived beyond the Euphrates and worshiped other gods.

familiar.text: And I took your father Abraham from the other side of the flood, and led him throughout all the land of Canaan, and multiplied his seed, and gave him Isaac.

modern.text: But I took your father Abraham from beyond the Euphrates and led him through all the land of Canaan, and I multiplied his descendants. I gave him Isaac,

modern.text: and to Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau Mount Seir to possess, but Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.

modern.text: When I brought your fathers out of Egypt and you reached the Red Sea, the Egyptians pursued them with chariots and horsemen as far as the Red Sea.

original.text: וָֽאוֹצִ֤יא אֶת אֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם וַתָּבֹ֖אוּ הַיָּ֑מָּה וַיִּרְדְּפ֨וּ מִצְרַ֜יִם אַחֲרֵ֧י אֲבוֹתֵיכֶ֛ם בְּרֶ֥כֶב וּבְפָרָשִׁ֖ים יַם סֽוּף

familiar.text: And when they cried unto the LORD, he put darkness between you and the Egyptians, and brought the sea upon them, and covered them; and your eyes have seen what I have done in Egypt: and ye dwelt in the wilderness a long season.

modern.text: So your fathers cried out to the LORD, and He put darkness between you and the Egyptians, over whom He brought the sea and engulfed them. Your very eyes saw what I did to the Egyptians. Then you lived in the wilderness for a long time.

verses.restored: I brought you to land of Amorite dwelling across Jordan; they fought with you, and I gave them into your hand. You possessed their land, and I destroyed them from before you.

familiar.text: And I brought you into the land of the Amorites, which dwelt on the other side Jordan; and they fought with you: and I gave them into your hand, that ye might possess their land; and I destroyed them from before you.

modern.text: Later, I brought you to the land of the Amorites who lived beyond the Jordan. They fought against you, but I delivered them into your hand, that you should possess their land when I destroyed them before you.

modern.text: After this, you crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The people of Jericho fought against you, as did the Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I delivered them into your hand.

modern.text: I sent the hornet ahead of you, and it drove out the two Amorite kings before you, but not by your own sword or bow.

familiar.text: And if it seem evil unto you to serve the LORD, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.

modern.text: But if it is unpleasing in your sight to serve the LORD, then choose for yourselves this day whom you will serve, whether the gods your fathers served beyond the Euphrates, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you are living. As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD!”

translation_notes: Joshua's final covenant begins with a surprising memory: Israel's ancestors beyond the River served other gods. Covenant identity is narrated as a history of transformation, not ethnic spiritual purity.
The speech retells Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Esau, Egypt, Exodus, wilderness, Balaam, Jordan, Jericho, and land gift as one Divine first-person memory.
Esau's possession of Seir is acknowledged, preserving a parallel land-gift tradition rather than making Israel the only people with received territory.

The claim that Israel dwells in cities it did not build and eats vineyards and olive groves it did not plant is theologically central and ethically dangerous: gift language must not erase prior labor or inhabitants.
'Choose this day' is a covenant appeal to accountable service, not a manipulative altar-call formula or coercive demand for instant religious conformity.
Joshua resists easy commitment by warning the people that service is weighty; this prevents cheap vows but should not be used for spiritual intimidation.
The covenant stone is a witness object under the oak at Shechem, not an idol or magical surveillance device.
The deaths and burials of Joshua, Joseph's bones, and Eleazar close the book through grief, memory, and continuity rather than conquest alone.
safety_note: Do not use Joshua 24 to coerce conversion, shame ancestral religion, erase prior inhabitants' labor, demand instant vows through fear, or treat covenant identity as ethnic purity. Center honest memory, chosen responsibility, humility about inherited homes and fields, witness without surveillance, and grief-filled continuity after leaders die.
